paper_title: What Does Neuro Mean to Cardio Investigating the Role of Clinical   Specialty Data in Medical LLMs
caption: Negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens between baseline Mistral-v0.2 and the same model further fine-tuned on each specialty data. Each group represents tokens categorized into different clinical specialties. Each color means that the same model is further fine-tuned on each specialty data.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the negative log-probabilities for clinically relevant tokens, comparing the baseline Mistral-v0.2 model against the same model fine-tuned on data from six distinct clinical specialties: Cardio, Gastro, Infect, Neuro, Obstetrics, and Pediatrics. The horizontal axis, labeled “Per-specialty terms,” lists these six specialties in order from left to right. The vertical axis, labeled “Negative log probability,” is scaled linearly from -22 to -27, with tick marks at regular intervals of one unit. Each specialty is represented by a group of six vertical bars, one for each fine-tuning condition, with the baseline Mistral-v0.2-Base model shown as a single light blue bar on the far left of each group. The remaining five bars within each group correspond to the five specialties, color-coded as follows: Cardio (light peach), Gastro (light orange), Infect (orange), Neuro (dark orange), Obstetrics (brown), and Pediatrics (dark brown). Within each group, the bars are arranged from left to right in the order of the specialties listed in the legend. The baseline Mistral-v0.2-Base bar is consistently the tallest (least negative) in each group, indicating the highest probability for the tokens it predicts. The bars for the fine-tuned models are generally shorter (more negative), indicating lower probabilities. The shortest bars (most negative) in each group correspond to the Neuro specialty, which is represented by the dark orange bars. The chart does not show any explicit sorting of the groups or individual bars beyond their positional order along the x-axis.
